Chicago woman shot five times by Border Patrol agent sues Trump administration

A woman who was shot five times by a Border Patrol agent while driving in Chicago last year has sued the Trump administration over the nonfatal incident. Actual Article Body:
A woman who was shot five times by a Border Patrol agent while driving in Chicago last year has sued the Trump administration over the nonfatal incident.

Marimar Martinez, 30, filed the lawsuit on Monday, arguing the federal government is liable for the agent’s “negligent acts” under the Federal Tort Claims Act. The law allows private citizens to sue the United States, as federal agents cannot be sued directly.

[Source 2 — www.foxnews.com] (URL: https://www.foxnews.com/outkick-culture/woman-sues-las-vegas-bar-injured-world-famous-gyrating-johnson-mechanical-member-bull):
Stated Claim / Post Context:
Woman sues Las Vegas bar claiming she was injured on 'World Famous Gyrating Johnson Mechanical Member Bull'

Amber Zabran is suing The Nerd bar in downtown Las Vegas after she was thrown from its mechanical bull ride, claiming she suffered serious injuries.

Actual Article Body:
An Illinois woman is suing a Las Vegas bar claiming that she was hurt during a ride on its "World Famous Gyrating Johnson Mechanical Member Bull ride." If it seems like an unnecessary use of words to you, that's because it is.

This "Gyrating Johnson" is nothing more than a mechanical penis that people attempt to ride. The woman, Amber Zabran, is suing for damages, reports 8 News Now, after she was thrown from Johnson during an attempt to ride it.

HBO's Kristen Ardigo falls from a mechanical bull at the after-party following the premiere of HBO's "Deadwood" at the Cabana Club in Hollywood, Calif., on June 6, 2006. (Getty Images)

Her complaint, filed in Clark County District Court last week, states she was injured when "her foot and/or ankle got caught under the main shaft area of the ride where there is a large cut-out section."
